survey: A flying saucer floating with no ground. The main disc is a wide, shallow brushed-metal cone with a dark tubular rim. It is seen from above at a moderate angle and rolled slightly, so the left side sits lower than the right. Twelve orange sphere lights sit along the rim. They are larger and spaced wider at the front and get smaller and closer together toward the sides and back, so they follow the rim's ellipse. A dark collar ring sits at the top of the cone, and a green glass dome sits in it. The dome shows a flat inner liquid line and a highlight on top. The view from above holds for both the disc and the rim. The underside is hidden, which matches that view. There is no ground contact to check.

errors.where: Dome and its collar ring on top of the saucer
errors.what: The disc is seen clearly from above and rolled to one side. The dome's collar ellipse is much flatter (about 1:4) than the rim ellipse (about 1:2.2) and sits almost level. Because of this the dome looks as if it is seen from closer to eye level and stands straight up instead of leaning with the disc's tilt. Its axis does not quite match the disc's axis.

fix: Seat the green glass dome squarely on the center of the saucer, with its axis perpendicular to the disc. Its base collar ring should be an ellipse with the same tilt and a similar openness to the saucer's outer rim, so the dome is seen from the same high three-quarter view as the disc.
